summary: Whiteface's 1909 summit station grew into a steel fire tower, dismantled in 1972 and re-erected at the Adirondack Museum in 1973.

facts.design: Steel lookout with a glass-enclosed cab; sources give 22 feet (1919) and about 50 feet (1942)
facts.status_note: Dismantled on the summit in 1972 and re-erected at the Adirondack Museum on Blue Mountain Lake in 1973.

visit.trail_note: The summit road was built in the 1930s and is open from May to October, per the marker page.

events.note: Summit observation station established in July 1909 with a pole frame and canvas tent; cost $1,559.31 per the 1910 state report; no tower at first
Sam Cheltham was fire observer until November 1, 1918, and was back at work by May 1919
Log-pole station replaced by a steel tower; the marker page and 1919 newspaper give 22 feet
George Marshall was the state fire observer on Whiteface
Five caddy boys damaged a window sash; the district ranger offered to call it square if they bought and delivered a new one, and two days later they did
CCC youths drilled the summit rock for steel poles for a new telephone line from the base to the tower
The state marker is dated 1935, and the marker page says a stone observation tower built that year replaced the steel tower; the 1942 and 1972 sources describe steel
A Coast and Geodetic Survey description calls the tower structural steel with a glass-enclosed cab, about 50 feet high
Riley Lawrence was fire observer on the state tower for the rest of the 1946 season
Tower dismantled in May 1972 under the state's wilderness plan; a newspaper item says the parts lay in about 200 pieces
Re-erected at the Adirondack Museum on Blue Mountain Lake as an outdoor exhibit

corrections.why: The record's agency field holds a fragment of the 1909 date. The Forest Lookouts page shows the Conservation Commission employed the 1919 fire observer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The marker and 1919 newspaper items date the steel tower to 1919. A 1972 newspaper calls the dismantled tower built in 1909, and a 1909 pole-frame station was there first. The 1919 steel tower is used here as the tower's build date.

notes_for_editor: This record covers the original summit site as the brief asks. The Adirondack Museum tower already has its own story and research file (us-ny-whiteface-mountain-at-adirondack-experience), and the two overlap. Height is unresolved: 22 feet (1919 items, marker) against about 50 feet (1942 Coast and Geodetic Survey); both are given in the design fact. The 1935 stone-tower claim on the marker conflicts with the steel-tower sources and is recorded as a conflict, not resolved. HMDB text includes visitor-written notes. No source read describes the summit as it is today. The DEC page was read directly, not from the search snippet. No new photos.
